name: Dynamic Text Recognition (DTR)
definition: Transcribe scene text from unstable egocentric views with head motion and viewpoint changes.
example: “I was walking fast and missed the phone number on that red sign. Can you tell me what it was?”

name: Dynamic Text Localization (DTL)
definition: Locate queried text regions in dynamic frames and describe where they appear in the observed scene.
example: “Where is the floor and unit number located on the billboard?”

name: Query-Guided Text Extraction (QTE)
definition: Select and extract relevant information from dense environmental text according to the user's query.
example: “How many years has this `Dianmao' restaurant been specializing in Peking Duck?”

name: Confirmation (CF)
definition: Verify the user's prior belief or memory using current visual-textual evidence.
example: “The sign says `Floor 4'. I'm in the mall now; this shop is on the 4th floor, right?”

name: Cross-Lingual Understanding (CLU)
definition: Interpret abbreviations, symbols, pinyin, or multilingual identifiers within the physical context.
example: “What does `DIANMAO' at the top of the sign represent in this context?”

name: Situated Semantic Interpretation (SSI)
definition: Interpret the semantic meaning of slogans, signs, or brand descriptions beyond literal recognition.
example: “What does the slogan `Unmatched in Beijing, Renowned Everywhere' imply about this brand?”

name: Wearer-Centered Situational Inference (WSI)
definition: Infer scene-level attributes or venue suitability by grounding text in the wearer's current situation.
example: “Based on the style and the `20-year' claim, is this a good place to treat friends to authentic local food?”

name: History-Conditioned Intent Inference (HII)
definition: Infer the wearer's current intent by combining previous scene-text observations with the current view.
example: “I'm tempted by the duck but have a meeting soon. Are there any `fast-eating' sets mentioned?”

name: Action-Trajectory Intent Prediction (AIP)
definition: Interpret the wearer's view trajectory to predict latent goals or possible next actions.
example: “I looked at the coffee shop sign and then the arrow sign. Am I trying to find the coffee shop?”

name: Structured Text Synthesis (STS)
definition: Integrate structured textual sources, such as menus, or floor boards, while preserving their layout logic.
example: “Translate the entire list of stores on this directory into English for me.”

name: Spatio-Temporal Navigation Reasoning (STN)
definition: Provide action guidance by integrating current location, target text, and movement cues over time.
example: “I see the `Floor 4' ad now. What is the fastest way for me to get to the actual store from here?”

name: Goal-Oriented Comparison (GOC)
definition: Compare text-described options across the video and select the one that matches the wearer's goal.
example: “Considering both `Professionalism' and `Price', is this shop a better choice than a fast-food outlet?”

name: Viewpoint Trajectory Description (VTD)
definition: Describe how the wearer's viewpoint changes over time relative to text-bearing signs or directories.
